title: Pre-Analysis Review — Temperature Compensated Probe Heat Standard and the Running Campaign

ata.title: Pitot and Static Heat — Probe Heat Computer

abstract: Closed review of the released temperature compensated monitoring standard, raised from the operator order on cold soak cautions, to decide what happens to its retrofit campaign now that a third monitoring standard is in pre-analysis.

sections.objective: Decide what should happen to the retrofit campaign for the temperature compensated monitoring standard now that a third standard, judging element health from thermal response rather than from resistance, has entered pre-analysis on the same computer. The review was raised from the operator order about cold soak cautions, whose fleet is part way through the campaign and asked directly whether it should continue paying for it or stop and wait, and the answer had to be defensible to the operators still deciding.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the campaign was allowed to run. The third standard supersedes the compensated logic but needs the same sense harness and the same supply pipe, so an aircraft that completes the current campaign is one step closer to it rather than one step wasted. That was the answer the operator needed and it is not obvious from either dossier. The open bulletin carries no forward note and had to be re-issued with one. The original fixed threshold standard is still installed on a small population that will need two embodiments in sequence, and the loading task will need a third branch.
sections.next_steps: Re-issue the bulletin effectivity with a forward note stating that the harness installed by this campaign is retained by the next standard. Write to the operators still running the campaign with the same statement. Identify the aircraft still at the fixed threshold standard and give them a two-step embodiment plan. Leave the third branch of the loading task to the candidate work order.

similarity_seeds: retrofit campaign part way through when a further standard appears
element health judged by thermal response rather than resistance

tasks.title: Establish what the third standard retains from this one
Review the open bulletin for a forward statement
Identify the population still at the fixed threshold standard

expected_findings.rationale: The candidate replaces the compensated judgement logic but keeps the supply pipe and the per-element sense harness that this standard installs. The retrofit already paid for is therefore retained, which is the fact that decides whether the running campaign is worth completing.
expected_findings.resolution: Statement issued to the operators still running the campaign; the supersession itself is declared by the candidate.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin says nothing about what comes after it. An operator reading it today cannot tell whether the standard it installs is the end of the line or a step, and several have asked. The effectivity itself is correct; the omission is the forward note.
expected_findings.resolution: Effectivity re-issued with a forward note naming the retained harness and supply pipe.

expected_findings.rationale: A small population never took this standard and is still at the fixed threshold logic. Those aircraft cannot go directly to the candidate, because the harness arrives with this standard and not with that one, so they need two embodiments in sequence.
expected_findings.resolution: Population identified from the embodiment records and given a two-step plan before the candidate cut-in.

expected_findings.rationale: The loading task decides which standard may be loaded from the hardware fitted, and its check is a visual inspection of the harness break-out. That check cannot discriminate the third standard, which depends on the supply solenoid rather than on anything visible.
expected_findings.resolution: Left to the candidate work order, which has to define a check the technician can actually perform.

type_data.conclusion: Validated. The campaign runs on, with a forward note added to the bulletin and a two-step plan for the aircraft still at the first standard.
